Miguel R.: Heads-up — swapping primary in 10. I'm running through handoff now, pinging the runbooks.
Jamie: ok, taking secondary for the window. any active pagers I should know about?
Miguel R.: None open right now. Last pager was a KV-cache spike earlier, resolved by warm restart (see runbook link below).
Miguel R.: Quick notes I want on the handoff: primary->secondary contact, current hotfix state, ongoing experiments that affect inference latency, any scheduled infra changes.
Jamie: got it. contact is @Sara for infra, @Kyle for model rollouts.
Sara: FYI we have a scheduled rollout tomorrow 03:00 UTC to add burst capacity in eu-west. Not happening during this shift but worth knowing if global routing sees capacity errors.
Kyle: model-rollout flag is off for production canaries — nothing in flight.
Miguel R.: Good. I'm adding these quick links: 
- KV cache troubleshooting: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache
- Primary pager playbook (fast path): https://internal.redwood/runbooks/primary-pager
- Route fallback matrix: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/routing-fallbacks
(please keep these open in case of a P1)
Jamie: quick checklist before I take over: 
1) Verify primary token rotation status 
2) Check slowhosts and recent p99 spikes in console 
3) Confirm alerting channels (pager, slack, email) are green
Miguel R.: yep — tokens valid until next week. p99 shows a single small blip at 20:13 UTC, no customer errors.
incident-bot: INCIDENT AUTO-TICKETING: No active incidents. Last incident #INC-4827 (kv-cache-thrash) closed 1765423312.
Jamie: ok taking primary at :00. leaving this thread with handoff notes.
Miguel R.: two quick mitigations to keep in your back pocket for KV increases: 
- command to drain a warm node: `infractl node drain --id <node-id> --reason "kv-warm-drain"`
- quick scale-up for dedicated: `dedicatectl scale --pool inference-primary --add-gpu 2`
(only run the second if latency SLOs are failing and owner approves)
Sara: if you see high error-rate with 503s, check endpoint routing: `curl -v https://console.internal.redwood/route-check?route=<route>` and verify fallback triggers in the routing-fallbacks doc.
Jamie: noted. Do we have any customer-impacting tests to run on takeover?
Miguel R.: run this smoke suite: `scripts/smoke/run_smoke.sh --short --route default` — should catch basic generation fails. It uses a small token budget.
Kyle: one more: watch the streaming connection count metric, that's a common early signal for degraded KV. metric: `streaming.conn.count` in the console. Thresholds in the playbook.
Jamie: copying live dashboards to my window. Anyone else seeing anything?
Sara: nothing on infra pager. I'll monitor during the swap for CPU pressure on the gpu-hosts.
Miguel R.: final: create a follow-up ticket if you had to run manual scale or node drains — tag `oncall/handback` and leave notes about why. That helps Optimize team tune autoscaling.
Jamie: taking primary now. If I get a pager I'll escalate to @Miguel and @Sara immediately.
oncall-rotation-bot: Reminder — next rotation ping scheduled for 12 hours.
Jamie: handoff complete. Leaving an action item: I'll run smoke after 2 minutes and post results here.
Jamie: smoke done: all checks passed, generation latency p95 within normals. :thumbsup:
Miguel R.: thanks — leaving you with one more tip: if you need to mute noisy non-customer alerts temporarily, use alertctl silence --id <alert-id> --until +10m and document why.
Kyle: thumbs up. thanks for clean handoff.
Jamie: noted, will document in the handback ticket.
Miguel R.: closing thread — reach out anytime.
